From 4d8be4bc94f74bb7d096e1c2e44457b530d5a170 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Qiushi Wu <wu000273@umn.edu>
Date: Wed, 27 May 2020 17:35:51 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] ACPI: CPPC: Fix reference count leak in
 acpi_cppc_processor_probe()

kobject_init_and_add() takes reference even when it fails.
If this function returns an error, kobject_put() must be called to
properly clean up the memory associated with the object. Previous
commit "b8eb718348b8" fixed a similar problem.

Fixes: 158c998ea44b ("ACPI / CPPC: add sysfs support to compute delivered performance")
Signed-off-by: Qiushi Wu <wu000273@umn.edu>
Cc: 4.10+ <stable@vger.kernel.org> # 4.10+
Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/acpi/cppc_acpi.c b/drivers/acpi/cppc_acpi.c
index f8184004294a..7a99b19bb893 100644
--- a/drivers/acpi/cppc_acpi.c
+++ b/drivers/acpi/cppc_acpi.c
@@ -846,6 +846,7 @@ int acpi_cppc_processor_probe(struct acpi_processor *pr)
 			"acpi_cppc");
 	if (ret) {
 		per_cpu(cpc_desc_ptr, pr->id) = NULL;
+		kobject_put(&cpc_ptr->kobj);
 		goto out_free;
 	}
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/acpi/cppc_acpi.c`**
- A new line was added to call `kobject_put(&cpc_ptr->kobj);` in the `acpi_cppc_processor_probe` function. This line is executed when the `kobject_init_and_add()` function fails (indicated by a non-zero `ret` value). This ensures that the reference count for the kobject is decremented properly, preventing a memory leak.

### Relationships
The modification addresses a reference count leak issue that arises when `kobject_init_and_add()` fails. The added line ensures that the memory associated with the kobject is cleaned up correctly by calling `kobject_put()`, which was not done previously. This change is related to a prior commit that fixed a similar issue, indicating a continued effort to maintain proper memory management in the ACPI CPPC driver. The patch is part of ongoing maintenance to ensure stability and reliability in the kernel's ACPI subsystem.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
ret = kobject_init_and_add(&cpc_ptr->kobj, &cppc_ktype, &cpu_dev->kobj, "acpi_cppc");
if (ret) {
    per_cpu(cpc_desc_ptr, pr->id) = NULL;
```
Reason:
The function `kobject_init_and_add()` takes a reference to the kobject even if it fails, but the code does not call `kobject_put()` to decrement the reference count when an error occurs. This results in a memory leak because the memory associated with the kobject is not released.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
kobject_put(&cpc_ptr->kobj);
```
Reason:
The addition of `kobject_put(&cpc_ptr->kobj);` ensures that the reference count is decremented when `kobject_init_and_add()` fails. This properly cleans up the memory associated with the kobject, preventing the memory leak.
